https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/19/magy.text: Menü Kereső Magyar: Vasárnap elkezdik visszakapcsolni Paks többi turbináját is, jövő héten már teljes lehet a kapacitás Belföld Szántó-Nagy Bálint Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Nem kell lekapcsolni a paksi atomerőmű jelenleg működő két turbináját, mert a várt szint fölött marad a vízszint – közölte Facebookon bejelentkezésében Magyar Péter. A miniszterelnök szerint az eddig felépült fenékküszöbnek és a bárkáknak köszönhetően 15 centit nőtt a víz. Vasárnaptól ütemezetten elkezdik visszakapcsolni az atomerőmű maradék hat turbináját, azaz a három korábban leállított blokkot is. Várhatóan jövő hét csütörtökön vagy pénteken már teljes, 2000 MW-os teljesítménnyel üzemel majd a paksi atomerőmű. Magyar azt mondta, hogy most már majdnem két hete megy a munka és óriási előrehaladást értek el a dolgozók. Az építkezésnek, azaz a bárkának, az épülő fenékküszöbnek és megnyitott ráckevei zsilipnek köszönhetően a Duna mélypontja a vártnál magasabban lesz. A miniszterelnök arról is beszélt, hogy voltak pillanatok, amikor nem tűnt ilyen jónak a helyzet, voltak reggelek, amikor úgy tűnt, hogy a két üzemelő turbinából is le kell majd állítani az egyiket. Magyar azt mondta, hogy az erőmű teljes kiesése havonta 50 milliárd forint pluszt jelent a költségvetésnek, illetve az adófizetőknek. A mostani építkezést eredetileg 6 milliárd forintra tervezték, de a felajánlásoknak köszönhetően ez az összeg kisebb lesz. „Csodálatos nemzeti összefogást láttunk” – összegzett Magyar Péter. Többször is megköszönte a Pakson dolgozó munkásoknak és szakembereknek a munkát, illetve azoknak is, akik felajánlásokkal segítették a munkát. „Ennél jobb hírt nem is kaphatott volna az 1026 éves Magyarország a nemzeti ünnep előtt” – mondta. „Reggel még nagyon nem ezt a képet láttuk, szinte csodák történtek” – mondta Gajdos László élő környezetért felelős miniszter, aki egész nap a helyszínen követte a munkálatokat. A fenékküszöb építése a négynapos hosszú hétvégén is folytatódik majd, a kieső magánfuvarozó cégek helyett a szállítást erre az időszakra a Honvédség veszi át. „Már csak órák, legfeljebb egy nap választ el bennünket a Duna várható legalacsonyabb vízállásától. Pakson most minden intézkedés számít” – összegezte a paksi helyzetet szerda délután Kapitány István . A gazdasági és energetikai miniszter ekkor azt mondta, hogy egyre nagyobb az esély rá, hogy az atomerőmű két működő turbináját üzemben tudják tartani. A bárkák alkalmazásáról és a fenékküszöb építéséről a kormány múlt szerdán döntött, hétfőre pedig már egészen másképp nézett ki a Dunának ezen szakasza. A munkálatokhoz Magyar szerint „kisebb noszogatásra”, de egészen távoli bányákból is ajánlottak fel követ, mások mellett Orbán Győző, Orbán Viktor apja is így tett , és a szakemberek azt mondták, a felajánlott mennyiség elegendő is lesz, csak a sürgős szállítás lehet a szűk keresztmetszet. Az elmúlt hetek forrósága, illetve a kialakult rekordalacsony vízállás miatt a hónap elején majdnem teljesen le kellett állítani az atomerőművet, mert a működéséhez szükséges hűtővizet a rendszer már alig-alig tudta kivenni a Dunából. http://www.euronews.com/2026/09/07/un-ri.text: The United Nations human rights chief demanded accountability for swelling numbers of deaths in US immigration custody on Monday, urging Washington to halt deportations to places where people face "irreparable harm."Speaking before the UN Human Rights Council, Volker Türk highlighted that "four more people have died in US immigration custody since my last update to this council" in June.That meant there had been "a total of 23 deaths in 2026 alone," he said, insisting that "there needs to be accountability for these deaths."US President Donald Trump has made combating illegal immigration a top priority of his second term, with authorities rounding up thousands of people and expanding detention centres.A joint report by Human Rights Watch and Physicians for Human Rights in June said that the rate of people dying in ICE custody has reached its highest level in over a decade amid Trump's crackdown.The UN rights chief also called out a range of other US immigration enforcement practices, including forcing migrant returns to dangerous places and to countries they had no connection to."I urge the United States to halt the return of people to places where they could suffer irreparable harm, including Haiti, and to ensure due process for all removals to third countries," he told the council.Türk also voiced alarm at the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agency's reported plans to "equip immigration agents with electric shock gloves" warning this would "increase the violence associated with their operations."The plan to purchase the shock gloves, which was first reported by the Associated Press news agency, calls for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), the ICE parent agency, to spend between $10-20 million (€8-17 million) on what are described as "distraction and de-escalation" devices.ICE has come in for criticism for a series of fatal shootings during enforcement operations, including those of two American citizens in Minnesota in January who were involved in anti-ICE protests.Critics have focused on the forceful tactics used by ICE agents in rounding up migrants and on an alleged lowering of the standards of training for new recruits.

https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/09/20/mosz.text: Menü Kereső Lángoló finomító, 400 kitelepített ember, 3 halott az ukránok vasárnapi moszkvai dróntámadása után Külföld Előd Fruzsina Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Videók is készültek a Moszkva elleni vasárnapi ukrán dróntámadás eredményéről, a Guardian által közzétett hírügynökségi felvételeken lángoló ipari létesítmény és sűrűn gomolygó füst látszik egy városi lakótelep fölött. Ukrajna az oroszországi választások harmadik napján több száz drónnal nagyszabású támadást indított Moszkva és környéke ellen. Az akcióban legalább három ember meghalt, és megrongálódott az a finomító, amelyet Volodimir Zelenszkij ukrán elnök Oroszország egyik „legfontosabb olajipari létesítményének” nevezett. Szergej Szobjanyin moszkvai polgármester nyilatkozata alapján 1600 drón indult el Oroszország felé, ebből 450 Moszkvát célozta. Zelenszkij ukrán elnök közlése szerint a támadás során használt fegyverek között volt úgynevezett Pelican is, amit eleinte rövid hatótávolságú ballisztikus rakétának tartottak, de források szerint később kiderült, hogy szárnyas drónról van szó. Az elnök nem közölt további részleteket, emiatt az ukrán média arról kezdett spekulálni, hogy ballisztikus rakétát is bevetettek, aztán a nap folyamán kétségek merültek fel a fegyver típusát illetően. Zelenszkij beszélt viszont arról, hogy Ukrajna hazai gyártású Flamingo robotrepülőgéppel is támadta Moszkvát. Ezt a nagy hatótávolságú fegyvert korábban már alkalmazták Oroszország belsejében található célpontok ellen. Ukrán és orosz Telegram-csatornák is tettek közzé olyan képeket a Guardian beszámolója szerint, amiken állításuk szerint a moszkvai régióban talált Flamingo rakéta roncsdarabjai láthatók, de ezeket az állításokat egyelőre független forrásokból nem sikerült ellenőrizni. A Guardian azt írja, az ukrán támadásokban három fő meghalt különböző helyszíneken, köztük egy 44 éves nő és egy idős férfi. Előző éjszaka Oroszország is támadta Ukrajnát , a kijevi régiós vezetés szerint négyen meghaltak a csapásokban, köztük egy anya és két hároméves gyereke. A vasárnapi moszkvai támadás nyomán tűz ütött ki egy 21 emeletes épületben, 400 embert kellett evakuálni – közölte Andrej Vorobjov moszkvai kormányzó. „Ezt a példátlan támadást egyértelműen azzal a céllal tervezték, hogy megzavarják a választásokat. Ez azonban nem sikerült az ellenségnek” – írta a Telegramon Szergej Szobjanyin a moszkvai eseményekre utalva. Kijev az elmúlt hónapokban nagyon sok dróntámadást indított Oroszország ellen, különösen az energetikai infrastruktúra ellen. Az ukránoknak jó okuk van a fosszilis szektort támadni, az energiahordozók exportja még mindig a Kreml fő bevételi forrása, amivel a háborús erőfeszítéseket finanszírozni tudja. Az ukrán csapások Oroszország olajfinomítási kapacitásának jelentős részét tönkretették, ami üzemanyaghiányt és üzemanyagár-emelkedést okozott az ország több régiójában, dízelből az export is megszűnt. Ez felfelé nyomja a világpiaci árakat, így már Donald Trump amerikai elnöknek sem tetszik annyira az ukrán stratégia, pedig korábban elismerően nyilatkozott róla. https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: Police found a second body while combing a property at Gurranang for clues after the first death. Photograph: Steven Saphore/AAP View image in fullscreen Police found a second body while combing a property at Gurranang for clues after the first death. Photograph: Steven Saphore/AAP New South Wales NSW man accused of murdering neighbour – and then murdering his relative two weeks later Police allege Nicholas Scott killed 79-year-old then ‘set upon’ 59-year-old relative who arrived at Gurranang to sort out estate Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australian Associated Press Wed 30 Sep 2026 01.20 EDT Last modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 01.24 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A man accused of murdering two members of a family on the same property a fortnight apart has faced court. The body of a 59-year-old man was found by police on Monday afternoon in a shed on a property at Gurranang, about 25km north of Grafton in northern New South Wales . The discovery was made as police combed the address for clues two weeks after a 79-year-old man’s body was found inside a home on the property. Det Supt Joe Doueihi on Wednesday said the alleged murder victims were related, adding the younger man came to NSW to help police with their investigation and to sort out the 79-year-old’s estate. He alleged the 59-year-old was “set upon” by a neighbour when he went to his deceased relative’s property. “It’s absolutely shocking for that family and for that community,” the homicide squad commander told reporters. Gurranang Gurranang Police alleged the neighbour – 32-year-old Nicholas Scott – was responsible for both murders. Scott was arrested at a hospital in Grafton, where he was receiving treatment, at about midday on Tuesday. He was taken to Grafton police station where he was charged with two counts of murder and stealing a motor vehicle. Scott briefly appeared in court on Wednesday morning and did not apply for bail. He will remain behind bars before returning to court in December. Supt Joanne Schultz told reporters on Tuesday the scene was extremely confronting and traumatic for first responders. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion “[Police] had attended the property to make further inquiries, they did not anticipate what they found,” she said. Police believe the 59-year-old man died in the past 24 to 48 hours, two weeks after police first came to the rural acreage to investigate the older man’s death. “The scene was not maintained for the entirety of that time,” Supt Schultz said. The deceased men appeared to have suffered similar injuries. Strike Force Faneel continues to investigate the deaths. https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/09/28/t.text: TMT Newswire GlobeNewswire JJP Biologics to Present Data Showing the Potential of Nebaprubart for Linear IgA Dermatosis (LAD) at Two Key Upcoming Scientific Conferences By GlobeNewswire September 28, 2026 10 Resize Small Medium Large Positive interim data from Phase Ib proof-of-concept trial will be presented at the IPPF Scientific Symposium on Pemphigus and Pemphigoid and at EADV Congress 2026 Data positions nebaprubart as a potential therapy across a broad range of IgA-mediated diseases Warsaw, Poland - September 28, 2026 - JJP Biologics, ("JJPBio" or the "Company") a clinical-stage, immune-focused biotech that engineers precision antibodies to correct derailed immune pathways that drive autoimmune diseases and cancer, today announced that data on nebaprubart, its investigational first-in-class anti-CD89 antagonist, will be presented as an oral presentation at the IPPF Scientific Symposium on Pemphigus and Pemphigoid being held 28-29 September in Lübeck, Germany, and as a poster presentation at the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology (EADV) Congress being held 30 September - 3 October in Vienna, Austria. Both presentations report interim findings from the Company's ongoing open-label Phase Ib proof-of-concept trial of nebaprubart in patients with linear IgA dermatosis (LAD), a rare autoantibody-mediated blistering skin disease. IPPF Scientific Symposium on Pemphigus and Pemphigoid, Lübeck, Germany Presenting author: Prof. Cezary Kowalewski, MD, PhD, sub-investigator of JJP Biologics' Phase 1b clinical trial, of the National Medical Institute of the Ministry of the Interior and Administration (PIM MSWiA), Warsaw Presentation title: Nebaprubart in Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis: Rapid Disease Control and Sustained Remission in an Open-Label Phase Ib Proof-of-Concept Study Date: 29 September 2026, 13:50-14:50 CEST Session: Session 6: Treatment of AIBD and Paediatrics. Get the latest news delivered to your inbox Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy . EADV Congress 2026, Vienna, Austria Advertisement Presenting author: Dawid Łyżwa, PhD, Head of Clinical Development at JJP Biologics Presentation Title: Nebaprubart in Linear IgA Dermatosis: Rapid Disease Control and Sustained Remission in an Open-Label Phase Ib Proof-of-Concept Study Date: 30 September 2026, 7:00AM CEST Session: Autoimmune Disorders Part II Sohail Ahmed, Chief Medical Officer of JJP Biologics, said: "We will share the interim data on nebaprubart for the first time at two leading autoimmune skin disease congresses, illustrating how the novel mechanism of our first-in-class anti-CD89 antagonist works in practice. Most current treatments for linear IgA dermatosis rely on broad immunosuppression, which carries its own burden of side effects and doesn't address the underlying mechanism. Nebaprubart is designed to block the IgA/CD89 interaction directly, and the presentations will show how that mechanism translates into patient outcomes." Prof. Cezary Kowalewski, MD, PhD, sub-investigator of JJP Biologics' Phase 1b clinical trial of nebaprubart for LAD, of the National Medical Institute of the Ministry of the Interior and Administration (PIM MSWiA), Warsaw, said: "Patients with linear IgA dermatosis have very limited options today. Corticosteroids and dapsone carry toxicity risks, and neither addresses the underlying mechanism. There is a need for a mechanism-specific alternative that gives patients and physicians a rational alternative to years of off-label, broadly immunosuppressive treatment. I look forward to presenting the data at IPPF and discussing what this mechanism could mean for how we treat this disease going forward." The Phase 1b trial (registered in the EU Clinical Trials Information System (CTIS) under EU Trial Number 2023-508661-33-00 ) is an open-label trial designed to evaluate safety and tolerability along with pharmacokinetic, immunogenicity, and exploratory efficacy measures including disease activity, blister formation, severity of pruritus and quality of life. The positive interim results from the trial were previously announced by JJPBio via a press release in June 2026. Starting from deep mechanistic insights, JJPBio engineers antibodies that are built-to-order, designed to restore immune balance and deliver better disease control for patients with significant unmet need, because we believe that we can do better for patients. JJPBio is the first company to generate clinical validation of the IgA/CD89 axis, establishing first-mover advantage in a disease area with broad implications across autoimmune conditions including IgA nephropathy, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, and celiac disease. Our immuno-oncology program targets the CD270/HVEM checkpoint pathway in cancer. Backed by the long-term, socially responsible capital of the Starak family and the Polpharma Group, JJPBio operates with the scientific freedom and financial stability to pursue mechanisms others simply cannot. Advertisement JJP Biologics: We restore. We don't deplete. We work smarter. About nebaprubart (JJP-1212) Nebaprubart is a first-in-class IgG4-κ CD89 antagonist that is being developed to treat a wide range of autoimmune, inflammatory, and fibrotic diseases where IgA antibodies are known to have significant pathogenic involvement (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, dermatitis herpetiformis, inflammatory bowel disease, IgA nephropathy, and IgA vasculitis). Nebaprubart was designated an Orphan Medicinal Product in October 2022 by the European Commission for the treatment of Linear IgA Disease. An open-label trial with nebaprubart for this indication is ongoing. Advertisement

https://dailyfreepress.com/10/05/21/2212.text: Categories: Lifestyle The importance of critical thinking, as told by Cristian Mungiu By Ava Malamut , Lifestyle Editor • October 5, 2026 Haein Shon Moral choices, societal pressures and difficult truths are a part of reality. Romanian filmmaker Cristian Mungiu forces us to think critically about these issues while entertaining observers in the process. “The film can be entertaining and still tell you something,” Mungiu said in a roundtable-style interview I attended. For his latest film “Fjord,” which won the filmmaker his second Palme d’Or at Cannes Film Festival, Mungiu serves as director, writer and producer. “I try to use these multiple positions to make sure that I’m coherent with the aims that the film has,” he said. “Fjord” follows an immigrant Romanian family living in Norway that faces an investigation and scrutiny from the local justice system. The film stars Sebastian Stan — yes, the Winter Soldier — speaking his native Romanian for the first time on screen, with Renate Reinsve — perhaps best known for her roles in “Backrooms” and “Sentimental Value” — portraying his wife. The film has already been well received on IMDb, Rotten Tomatoes and Letterboxd, despite not being released until Oct. 9. It’s ranked high on my own Letterboxd — 4.5 stars out of 5 — and I’m quite the film nerd. The intersection of reality and perception that is explored in this film is not only incredibly fascinating, but requires one to form their own judgment. Mungiu said his films are “a kind of fiction following the pattern of reality” and added that “facts in life do not come interpreted.” My mother always says life is all about perspectives, and this movie gives viewers an opportunity to form their own. Mungiu was born in Iași, Romania in 1968. He originally worked as a teacher, photographer and journalist in written press, radio and television. He started publishing short stories in periodicals in 1987. His journalistic background shows in the film’s impartial approach, which fits given that the idea for “Fjord” grew from real-life welfare cases. “I start from these pre-existing stories because I see in them the potential of speaking about something bigger than meets the eye when the press relates about that story,” he said. In speaking about the connections between “Fjord” and his 2022 film “R.M.N.,” he explained the throughline of the pair — tackling issues of xenophobia — and how “Fjord” is a “reverse of the paradigm.” “I thought after making [R.M.N.] that it would be interesting to see what happens in a society when the conservatives are the minority,” Mungiu said. Conservatism, coupled with religious differences, isolate the protagonists of “Fjord”. His films have now won four of the major awards at Cannes Film Festival, two of which were the most coveted, the Palme d’Or. He will be honored Oct. 11-12 at the Coolidge Corner Theatre with the 2026 Coolidge Impact Award, inaugurated last year by Iranian director Jafar Panahi. Mungiu’s work is often classified as Romanian New Wave, a globally acclaimed film movement characterized by stark realism, dark deadpan humor and minimalist storytelling that emerged in the mid-2000s. That said, Mungiu’s style is distinctive for its widescreen compositions with minimal camera movement and busy frames. “The idea is that you’re always trying to build up a match between the theme of the film, the evolution of the characters, the reasons for which they behave in a given way and the looks of the film,” he said. “It’s not just the cinematography. It’s also the scenery, which is very important.” I hope to one day take his masterclass, and maybe even have a film at the same festival. Mungiu’s work and philosophy serve as a reminder to us all to never stop being curious about the world around us. https://www.dw.com/en/czechia-braces-for.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5POMX Prefer DW on Google 'Strike — For a free press, free media' Many in Czechia fear that the government's plans to change the way public media is funded will undermine the independence of Czech Television and Czech Radio Image: Katerina Sulova/CTK Photo/IMAGO Advertisement Hundreds of thousands of people are expected to rally in Prague this weekend to protest the Czech government's bid to ram a bill to reform public media funding through parliament in a surprise overnight session in October. The right-populist coalition headed by Prime Minister Andrej Babis fast-tracked the first of three readings of the legislation, which culminated in a vote of approval at 4:36 a.m. on October 24. The bill has already provoked numerous demonstrations and strikes across the country, but Sunday's gathering in the capital's Letna park is likely to be by far the largest to date. What's in the bill? Under the government's proposal, the license fee model that currently funds Czech Television (CT) and Czech Radio (CRo) would be scrapped, and the broadcasters would be funded directly from the state budget. The three parties in the coalition — Babis's centrist ANO, the far-right SPD, and radical conservative Motorists, whose voter bases tend to be less affluent — insist that the license fee is an unfair tax. Crowds protested outside parliament while inside, the government pushed through the first reading of the controversial media funding bill on the night of October 23/24 Image: Michal Kamaryt/CTK Photo/IMAGO The parties argue that the new arrangement, which would see funding for CT and CRo cut by around 15% in the first year, would make the two more efficient. They also point out that several other European Union states have made similar changes. What are the objections to the bill? Critics have angrily dismissed these justifications. Opposition parties, civil society organizations and international watchdogs accuse the government of seeking to undermine the independence of the broadcasters, whose critical reporting has long irked ANO and the SPD in particular. Analysts point out that while models in other EU states include guarantees of long-term financial stability and editorial independence, the Czech government proposal offers neither. CT and CRo have warned that the reduced budget included in the bill will mean programming- and staff cuts . When the first publication of the proposed bill was met with protests over the summer, Vaclav Stetka of the European New School of Digital Studies told DW that such "dramatic budget cuts represent an act of cultural vandalism." There has also been condemnation of the restriction of the parliamentary debate amid the fast-tracking of the bill. The protests continued in the days after the late-night vote in parliament Image: Michael Heitmann/dpa/picture alliance "The confrontational approach, the attempts to limit parliamentary debate and the government's rhetoric towards journalists and critics have all contributed to the public backlash," Otto Eibl, political scientist at Masaryk University in Czechia 's second city Brno, told DW. What has happened since the bill was fast-tracked? The backlash was immediate. Crowds picketed parliament through the night as the government pushed through the first reading of the bill. Since then, multiple rallies have taken place in cities and towns across the country. Many of these protests were led by students and joined by unions, Churches and representatives of educational and cultural institutions. CT and CRo staff called a strike in early November, disrupting the country's TV and radio schedules. Sunday's protest is set to up the ante. It will take place two days before the anniversary of the start of the Velvet Revolution, which ultimately brought down communism in what was then Czechoslovakia in 1989. The civil society group Million Moments for Democracy, which is organizing Sunday's rally, brought an estimated 300,000 onto the streets to protest during Babis's first term as prime minister in 2019 and more than 200,000 earlier this year . Why has the reaction been so strong? The government's sudden bid to push through the proposal reflects impatience to deliver on a core pledge made ahead of the October 2025 election, as well as the longstanding ambition of the prime minister, who was stymied in his attempt to engineer control of CT's governing council during his first term in power in 2017–21. 'For you, not for politicians' — Public broadcasters are seen by many in Czechia as cornerstones of democracy Image: Eva Korinkova/REUTERS Vaclav Stetka notes that repeated assaults on public media by Czech governments past and present reflect a particular political culture across Europe's post-communist states. "The political elite has never accepted the independence of public media," he asserted. In Czechia, however, the public broadcasters have earned special status as cornerstones of democracy . That standing was forged in what became known as the "Czech TV crisis" of 2000–01, when an occupation of CT's studios by staff and mass protests forced the government of the day to back down on a bid to wrest control. "The fight over the public service media has become a symbol of the defense of liberal democratic values and institutions," Eibl said. How has the government reacted? As anger has swelled, the government has sought to calm the situation. Babis has said that a new proposal, which would see public media funding moved off budget and editorial independence guaranteed, would be drawn up and made available for a full and open debate. During the November 3 strike at Czech Television, hosts read the news in front of a darkened newsroom Image: Eva Korinkova/REUTERS However, critics remain unimpressed, noting a lack of any detail and the fact that other members of the government appear determined to remain on course. Million Moments for Democracy has insisted the pressure must continue. "Words are worth nothing," the group said. "While people stand up for independent media, the government continues to act as if it owns the country." What are the potential risks for the government? With little sign that the opposition will dissipate, the government faces a choice. It has the parliamentary majority it needs to push the bill through and defeat any likely vetoes from the upper house Senate and President Petr Pavel . But this could come at a cost. Polls suggest political support for the government has been weakened and could diminish further if the protests expand to include growing frustrations over the cost of living and housing, as happened recently with student-led protests in France and other European countries . "The real risk for the government is that the media issue becomes a lightning rod for broader dissatisfaction," said Martin Vokalek of the Prague-based EUROPEUM Institute for European Policy. Could things turn violent? Babis is aware of the danger. Public opposition to the government's plans for Czech public media are nothing new: this demonstration outside Czech Television in June called for the dismissal of Culture Minister Oto Klempir and expressed support for the country's public media Image: Ondrej Deml/CTK/picture alliance The PM announced that he will not attend the Velvet Revolution anniversary celebrations on November 17, which are hugely symbolic, in the hope that his absence might "calm the tense situation." However, there's little concern that the Czech protests could descend into violence. Analysts note that the anger in Czechia remains tightly focused on the public media proposal and continues to be expressed in a similar way to the seismic events of the country's modern history. "I would not expect French-style scenes," Vokalek told DW, noting that the same "large, peaceful and civic Czech protest culture," which gave the Velvet Revolution and 1993's Velvet Divorce from Slovakia their name, is still strong.
